deltas.subject: Resolve Kraken spot reports spelled with the pair altname (#5034)
deltas.review_summary:
Resolve Kraken spot reports spelled with the pair altname (#5034)
    
    Kraken spells a spot pair two ways. `AssetPairs` keys it `XXBTZEUR`, which becomes the
    instrument `raw_symbol`, while `OpenOrders` and `TradesHistory` report the altname
    `XBTEUR`. `get_instrument_by_raw_symbol` compared only the key, so on a legacy-named pair
    the lookup missed and the report was dropped inside a successful, shorter return.
    Reconciliation never adopted the order, and nothing was logged.
    
    Record each `altname` against its `AssetPairs` key when instruments are requested, and
    resolve by key first and altname second so a key is never shadowed. The altname is not
    derivable from a cached instrument, because `normalize_spot_symbol` rewrites Kraken's
    currency codes; and `OpenPositions` returns the key while the order and trade reads return
    the altname, so both spellings have to resolve.
    
    Return an error when a report cannot be resolved, at all three affected sites (open orders,
    closed orders, trade history), matching the existing `OpenPositions` behaviour. A silently
    shorter list reads to reconciliation as "the order does not exist", which is worse than a
    failed read.
    
    `test_mass_status_captures_collection_start` now connects its spot client first, so
    instruments are cached as they are on the production path. Its assertions are unchanged.
    
    * Warn and preserve Kraken spot historical reports that cannot resolve
    
    The adapter guide classifies a record whose instrument is missing by scope: an in-scope
    open order or position report returns an error, while an in-scope closed or historical
    record is logged as a warning. Returning an error for a historical row aborted the whole
    read, so one delisted or expired instrument could withhold every other record it returned,
    preventing startup or blocking a single-order probe over unrelated history.
    
    Log a warning naming the instrument and skip the row for closed orders and trade history,
    preserving the records that resolve. Open orders continue to return an error, since a
    dropped open order report is indistinguishable from an order the venue never had.
    
    Both regression tests pair an unresolved row with a valid one and assert a control first:
    the identical payload with every pair resolvable returns both rows, so the skipped row is
    well-formed and is skipped only because its pair cannot be resolved.

deltas.subject: Preserve ExecutionEngine handoffs in later submit commands (#5020)
deltas.review_summary:
Preserve ExecutionEngine handoffs in later submit commands (#5020)
    
    An order handed to an execution client keeps its INITIALIZED (or
    RELEASED) status until the adapter's OrderSubmitted arrives, so a
    later SubmitOrderList that failed validation (for example an invalid
    custom position ID under NETTING) denied it along with the fresh
    members, dropping its later venue events because no DENIED ->
    SUBMITTED/ACCEPTED/FILLED transition exists. A valid later list
    naming the same order also routed it to the client a second time.
    
    The engine now records each successful client handoff until the
    order's first status transition is applied, and treats such an order
    as ineligible for any later submit command:
    
    - A repeated SubmitOrder is skipped with a warning and never
      reaches the client
    - A SubmitOrderList naming the order is denied without reaching the
      client: ORDER_LIST_DENIED applies only to its eligible members,
      while the dispatched order keeps its lifecycle and later events
    - External-client handoffs are recorded after publishing, and the
      record is checked independently of the cache because those
      orders are not cached by the engine
    - Reset clears the record, so the same order ID reaches the client
      again on a new command
    
    Add regression tests for later invalid and valid lists before and
    after the first OrderSubmitted event, duplicate submit commands, the
    external-client path, and resubmission after reset, each asserting
    the client is not invoked again and the original order's later
    events apply. Document submit eligibility in the execution policies.
    
    Fixes #4944

deltas.subject: Declare the lookback window on Kraken bounded mass status (#5043)
deltas.review_summary:
Declare the lookback window on Kraken bounded mass status (#5043)
    
    Kraken spot and futures apply a lookback cutoff to historical queries
    without declaring it on the mass status, preventing the engine from
    applying its bounded-history rules.
    
    Record the shared cutoff with `ExecutionMassStatus::set_report_window`
    and mark the set incomplete when order or fill records cannot be resolved
    or parsed. Warn with the symbol when futures records cannot be resolved.
    Keep public report signatures and the Python API unchanged by carrying
    completeness through crate-private methods.
    
    Derive the cutoff in `UnixNanos` using saturating arithmetic to avoid
    overflow and pre-epoch conversion panics.
    
    Document that the declared cutoff enables bounded-history rules, while
    completeness qualifies the returned set. Position records remain outside
    the completeness flag, and unresolved futures positions are still skipped.
    
    Add spot and futures regression tests for declared cutoffs and unresolved
    fills, plus a spot fill parse-failure test. Use successful controls to
    confirm that skipped records drive the incomplete result.

deltas.subject: Scope Kraken cancel-all and batch selected cancellations (#5044)
deltas.review_summary:
Scope Kraken cancel-all and batch selected cancellations (#5044)
    
    Spot sent an account-wide `CancelAll` for an unsided request even though the command
    names an instrument, so it could cancel orders on instruments the request never named.
    Side-filtered requests on both clients sent one HTTP cancel per selected order rather
    than reusing the explicit-id batch path.
    
    Spot now selects the matching open orders for the requested instrument, with or without
    a side filter, and cancels them by explicit venue id through the batch path. Futures
    keeps its symbol-scoped bulk cancellation for unsided requests and uses the batch path
    for side-filtered ones.
    
    Each generated cancel carries the owning strategy of the order it targets and the
    cancel-all command id as its correlation, and the existing batch path keeps the venue
    chunk limit and leaves aggregate or ambiguous responses to reconciliation.
    
    * Reach submitted Kraken orders from a scoped cancel-all
    
    Selecting only open orders skipped an order the venue may already have accepted while
    the cache still records it as `Submitted`. The account-wide cancellation this replaced
    reached those, so the scoped selection silently stopped covering them.
    
    Select in-flight orders alongside open ones for the requested instrument, deduplicated
    by client order id, on both clients. `is_open` already covers `PendingCancel` and
    `PendingUpdate`, so `Submitted` is the state this adds.
    
    Also extend the futures side-filter test to assert the submitted ids, that the opposite
    side and another instrument are excluded, and that a per-order rejection carries the
    strategy owning the order.
    
    * Send Kraken spot batch cancellations under the documented fields
    
    Kraken's `CancelOrderBatch` keys transaction IDs and client order IDs separately:
    `orders` accepts transaction IDs and user references, while a client order ID must
    be sent under `cl_ord_ids`. The batch path put both into `orders`, so a cancel
    without a venue order ID could not match at the venue.
    
    This mattered little while only accepted orders were selected, but scoped cancel-all
    now also selects submitted orders, which have no venue order ID yet, so that fallback
    became the common path.
    
    Split the identifiers into their documented fields, chunking before the split so the
    venue limit of 50 still counts both together. The single-cancel path already made this
    distinction, as does the futures batch path.

deltas.subject: Cap Kraken spot report pagination (#5062)
deltas.review_summary:
Cap Kraken spot report pagination (#5062)
    
    The closed-order and fill reads advance an offset until the venue returns an empty
    page, with no upper bound. A venue that kept returning a non-empty page would leave
    the read spinning: the fill read would consume the whole `timeout_reconciliation`
    budget and fail startup, and the closed-order read would not return to its caller.
    
    Stop both loops after 500 pages, matching the cap OKX already applies to its own
    pagination, and report a set cut short that way as incomplete rather than silently
    truncating it. Kraken Futures is unaffected; it does not paginate by offset.
    
    Each loop has a regression test that serves the same non-empty page on every
    request, so the read can only return by way of the cap, and each asserts the exact
    page count against a control that terminates on an empty page. The fill read is
    reached through startup mass status; the closed-order read is reached by requesting
    non-open orders, since spot mass status asks for open orders only.
    
    Closes #5061

deltas.subject: Scope Postgres cache by trader (#5070)
deltas.review_summary:
Scope Postgres cache by trader (#5070)
    
    The Postgres cache loads and flushes trading state without trader
    scoping, so nodes sharing a database can reconcile each other's state
    or erase it on startup. Client order and position IDs are only unique
    per trader, which also allows collisions in snapshots, index entries,
    and position fill history.
    
    Require a trader ID for Postgres cache connections and scope trading
    loads, index operations, position-event replacement, and flushes by
    trader. Qualify order and position snapshot keys and the order-position
    index with the trader ID. Preserve shared reference data, market data,
    and other shared tables during a flush.
    
    Stamp account events with the writing trader because AccountState
    carries no trader ID. Reject account and order event UUID conflicts
    across traders, preserving the original row and returning an error.
    Account events awaiting assignment remain unchanged.
    
    Migrate existing snapshot and index keys, resolving index ownership
    from position fills or order events. Stop migration and report rows
    whose owner cannot be resolved. Require explicit assignment of legacy
    account events with `nautilus database assign-account`; cache
    connections fail until assignment is complete. The command connects
    directly and remains usable while cache connections are blocked.
    
    Propagate flush errors through Cache::flush_db and
    ExecutionEngine::flush_db so a failed flush_on_start stops node startup.
    
    Cover shared-ID isolation, event conflicts, migration, and distinct
    account states across restart and either trader's flush. Ensure the
    account-assignment test cleans up before reconnect assertions, and
    document the required migration steps.
    
    Closes #5050.

deltas.subject: Optimize position replay duplicate fill checks (#5096)
deltas.review_summary:
Optimize position replay duplicate fill checks (#5096)
    
    The Postgres and Redis position loaders and the event store fill replay
    check each replayed fill with Position::trade_ids().contains(). That
    method rebuilds a sorted Vec of every trade ID in the current cycle on
    each call, so replaying a position that stays open over n fills costs
    O(n^2 log n).
    
    Check the Position.trade_ids set instead, as the execution engine
    already does. Every Position mutation updates it together with events,
    so it holds the same trade IDs and the duplicate decision is unchanged.

    The duplicate trade check in apply_orderless_flip_fill had no test:
    with it disabled, all event store tests still passed. Replay a
    duplicate of an earlier reducing fill that exceeds the remaining
    quantity, which must stay the idempotent no-op rather than a flip.

deltas.subject: Fix canceled FOK orders consuming book liquidity (#5106)
deltas.review_summary:
Fix canceled FOK orders consuming book liquidity (#5106)
    
    With liquidity_consumption enabled, the matching engine debits consumed
    book and trade liquidity while determining fills, before apply_fills
    checks FOK completeness. A FOK that is then canceled for insufficient
    liquidity has filled nothing but still leaves the liquidity marked as
    consumed, so later orders against the same book state cannot fill it.
    
    Capture the consumption state before a FOK fill attempt and restore it
    when the final fills cannot satisfy the order. The FOK completeness
    check is shared with apply_fills so both decisions use the same
    normalized fill quantities.
    
    * Make FOK consumption restore proportional to crossed levels
    
    The FOK consumption checkpoint cloned the full consumption map for the
    order side on every FOK attempt. Those maps only clear on reset, so the
    cost grew with the length of a run.
    
    Replace the checkpoint with a journal that apply_liquidity_consumption
    fills with the prior value of each level it touches. A canceled FOK
    reverts the journaled levels in reverse, which also removes levels the
    attempt inserted and keeps the original map order, and restores the
    prior trade consumption. Non-FOK orders and runs without
    liquidity_consumption record nothing.

deltas.subject: Reject running a disposed backtest node (#5086)
deltas.review_summary:
Reject running a disposed backtest node (#5086)
    
    BacktestNode::run disposed the engine after a successful run when
    dispose_on_completion was set, the default, but kept it in the engine
    map, so a second run skipped the auto-build and ran the disposed
    engine, returning a result with carried-over iterations and an empty
    account summary. BacktestNode::dispose cleared the map instead, so a
    later run silently built a fresh engine.
    
    Record disposal on the node, from a completed run and from dispose,
    and return an error from run and build before touching an engine. A
    run that failed with raise_exception disabled leaves its engine
    undisposed and can still run again.
    
    Coded by an LLM.

deltas.subject: Restore cache-open orders into the sandbox matching engine on start (#5046)
deltas.review_summary:
Restore cache-open orders into the sandbox matching engine on start (#5046)
    
    SandboxExecutionClient::start now mirrors SimulatedExchange::load_open_orders:
    read every cache-open order for the client's venue, ensure a matching engine
    for its instrument, and hand the order to process_order. The engine's
    accept_order idempotency skips the OrderAccepted event when the order is
    already Accepted, so the strategy sees no spurious events for a restored
    resting order.
    
    Without this, a LiveNode restart with a durable cache and a
    SandboxExecutionClient left every resting order stuck: the cache reported it
    Accepted, but no matching engine held it, so it could neither fill nor
    cancel. On a paper node this silently disarmed every resting stop-loss and
    take-profit across restarts.
    
    Adds a sandbox integration regression that seeds an Accepted limit into the
    cache, starts the client, and verifies the matching engine is populated and
    a cancel resolves cleanly without OrderCancelRejected or duplicate
    OrderAccepted.
    
    Resolves #5023

deltas.subject: Scope Kraken reads by resolved instrument ID (#5129)
deltas.review_summary:
Scope Kraken reads by resolved instrument ID (#5129)
    
    Seven scoped-read filters compared a cached instrument's `raw_symbol` against
    the venue's row spelling. Kraken spells a spot pair two ways, the `AssetPairs`
    key used as `raw_symbol` and the altname used by `OpenOrders`, `ClosedOrders`
    and `TradesHistory`, so a read scoped to such a pair dropped that pair's own
    records. The comparison also sat inside a cached-instrument lookup, so when the
    requested instrument was not held the filter was skipped and the read returned
    every instrument's records.
    
    Resolve each row and compare instrument IDs, and return early when the requested
    instrument is not held. Spot and futures IDs share the `KRAKEN` venue, so a
    futures ID reaching the spot client, or the reverse, now matches nothing.
    
    The alias index was recorded only while fetching `AssetPairs`, leaving a client
    fed through the cache APIs unable to resolve an altname-spelled row. Carry the
    altname on the instrument, so the cache APIs can index it without the fetch.
    
    Distinguish a row that resolved to another instrument from one that did not
    resolve at all, so an unresolvable row marks the set incomplete rather than
    yielding an empty set reported as complete.
    
    * Address review on Kraken scoped reads
    
    Skip an unresolvable row on a scoped read rather than marking the set
    incomplete, as the futures position read already does, and limit the
    documented open-order failure to unscoped reads.
    
    Correct the cache-supplied test's comments, which still described a client
    with no altname index, and move the altname key import to the module's
    import block.

deltas.subject: Fix duplicate and out-of-order bars accumulating in Cache (#5109)
deltas.review_summary:
Fix duplicate and out-of-order bars accumulating in Cache (#5109)
    
    Cache::add_bar and Cache::add_bars keep each bar_type series newest-first: newer bars are pushed, older ts_events are skipped (still delivered in the response), and an equal ts_event replaces the front bar for time bars. Non-time bars can legitimately share a ts_event (Renko bricks, volume bars), so all bars at a timestamp are kept. This restores the v1 older-bar check missing in v2 and stops overlapping historical requests from putting stale bars at the front.
    
    Request-aggregated bars are delivered only through the cache, so their chain handler now uses Cache::add_bar_historical to insert each bar at its ordered position instead of skipping it behind a newer live bar. Sequence validation is bypassed there: both checks compare against the latest cached bar.
    
    Also drop the `Bar.is_revision` parity-plan comment from the data engine, now covered by the insertion rule.
    
    Fixes #5083

deltas.subject: Add Kraken average entry price to spot margin position reports (#5065)
deltas.review_summary:
Add Kraken average entry price to spot margin position reports (#5065)

Spot margin position reports were built with `avg_px_open: None` although
`OpenPositions` returns `cost` and `vol` for every lot. Reconciliation cannot
open a position from a report without an entry price when the cache holds no
order or fill history for it.

Track the long and short notionals alongside the netted quantity and derive the
entry average for the side that survives netting, weighted by the volume still
open. Averaging the sides separately keeps the reported price one the surviving
exposure was actually opened at.

Kraken Futures already passes the venue price through
`parse_futures_position_status_report`, so it needs no change. The remaining
`None` entry averages on the spot side are the synthetic FLAT reports and the
wallet-balance-derived cash positions, neither of which has an entry price.

Closes #5064

* Mark Kraken spot margin entry averages as opening only

The engine can now distinguish a venue average that matches a netting position
from one that only prices a position opened from flat. Kraken closes spot
margin lots FIFO and drops a fully closed lot from `OpenPositions`, so after a
partial close the average describes the surviving lots, not the opening fills.

Mark those reports `AvgPxReconciliation::OpeningOnly`. Reconciliation then uses
the average to open a position from flat and never compares it with the cached
netting average, which is what previously left a report unresolved.

Futures keeps the default: that endpoint reports one netted position per symbol
rather than lots, and Kraken documents its price as the average entry price.

deltas.subject: Fix strategy-scoped cancel-all skipping local orders (#5120)
deltas.review_summary:
Fix strategy-scoped cancel-all skipping local orders (#5120)

Include locally active orders in strategy-scoped cancel-all selection.
An order submitted earlier in the same handler can still be INITIALIZED
while its submit command is queued, so the existing open, emulated,
in-flight, and execution-algorithm queries miss it. Use the cache's
locally active index and pass matching orders through the existing
filtered, sorted, and deduplicated per-order cancellation path.

Handle deferred submission and acceptance in the matching engine. With
use_message_queue=false, an accepted order can still appear INITIALIZED
or RELEASED in the cache when a cancel arrives. Previously, cancellation
could remove it from the matching book without emitting OrderCanceled,
leaving the cache ACCEPTED once the deferred events arrived. Contingent
cancellation could also skip an OCO sibling in that state.

Before direct or contingent cancellation, apply deferred submission to
the local snapshot of an order the engine holds, and acceptance if it
is in the matching core. OrderCanceled then follows the deferred events
through the same handler. Reject a direct cancel if those transitions
fail, leaving the order in place. Queued mode uses the cached state.

Track parked OTO children in pending_oto_order_ids when their parent is
on the same instrument. These children wait outside the matching core
until the parent triggers them. Tracking them lets immediate-mode
cancellation recognize them while their submission events are deferred,
so canceling a bracket entry also cancels its parked children. Direct
cancellation of a parked child also cancels its OUO sibling, matching
queued-mode behavior. Remove children when triggered or canceled, and
clear the set on reset.

Record rejected OTO parents until their rejection reaches the cache.
This lets children processed during the same deferred command see the
rejection and become REJECTED instead of remaining SUBMITTED and
blocking a market exit. Purge the record once the cache reflects the
rejection, and clear it on reset.

Keep children parked while their parent can still fill. A market parent
never enters the matching core, and an order list can place a child
before its parent, so absence from the core does not establish rejection.
Preserve full-trigger behavior for market entries that fill in several
steps, and leave cross-instrument child routing unchanged.

Share OrderSubmitted construction between event generation and snapshot
updates. Add regression coverage for deferred cancellations, parked
bracket children, rejected parents, child-before-parent ordering, and
multi-step market entries under full triggering.
deltas.no_impact_rationale: Enforces tick increments at simulated-order boundaries; inspected guidance does not recommend submitting off-tick prices.

deltas.review_summary:
Align indicator warmup and conventions with standard definitions (#5144)

Align indicator warmup, seeding, and output conventions with standard
definitions. Use mean-based moving-average seeds, keep SMA and WMA at
zero until their windows fill, seed AMA from the previous price, and
truncate sqrt(period) in HMA. RSI defaults to Wilder smoothing on
[0, 100], and RSI, CMO, and VHF exclude the artificial first change.
Flat windows return neutral values, including 50 for both Stochastics
lines.

Correct the OBV, KVO, VolatilityRatio, VWAP, and DirectionalMovement
calculations. KVO uses high - low as its daily measurement and
high + low + close to determine trend. CMO divides before scaling.
Add MACD signal and histogram outputs, selectable ROC modes, Bollinger
standard deviation, and per-line Ichimoku availability. ZScore uses
population deviation.

Share sums, rolling moments, regression, and validation in an indicator
support module. Reseed shifted sums when the window mean drifts more
than 32 standard deviations from the reference, centering on the window
value closest to the mean. This preserves tiny nonzero variances and
shifts flat windows to exact zeros. LinearRegression returns NaN r2
only for flat windows, preserving valid finely priced fits. Remove
overflow-only fallbacks that bounded price and quantity inputs cannot
reach.

Ignore invalid candles and non-finite inputs without changing state.
Use checked Pressure and KeltnerPosition constructors so invalid ATR
floors and multipliers raise ValueError from Python. Preserve no-op
quote and trade handlers for ATR, VolatilityRatio, VHF, and RVI. Keep
the public checked constructors and MAX_PERIOD constants, with window
periods supported up to 16,777,216.

Update Python bindings and stubs, make RateOfChangeMode hashable, and
move the AX examples, tutorial, and panel renderer to RSI thresholds
of 30 and 70. Pin indicator behavior with exact reference values,
restored flat-price coverage, independent VIDYA CMO periods, and
small-variance regressions. Use valid candles and assert populated
state before resetting KVO, DM, Pressure, and the Keltner indicators.

deltas.subject: Use standard currency codes across the Kraken adapter (#5155)
deltas.review_summary:
Use standard currency codes across the Kraken adapter (#5155)

Kraken uses different codes for the same asset across instruments, balances,
and fees. Since currencies compare by code, those entries do not match.
Replace single-character X/Z stripping with an explicit alias table shared
by instruments, balances, fees, symbols, and currency configuration. Pass
unlisted codes through unchanged, preserving valid prefixes in codes such
as XTZ, ZRX, and XAUT.

Book fees in the currency reported by the venue, falling back to the quote
currency when none is reported. This handles inverse futures fees charged
in the base currency. When the reported code matches a currency carried
by the instrument, retain that definition and its precision.

Sum futures holdings per standard currency code across separately funded
cash, single-collateral, and flex wallets, then emit one balance per currency
in code order. This removes hash-map-dependent balance selection. Exclude
flex USD collateral when portfolioValue already includes it, and exclude
contract-symbol position entries from single-collateral currency balances.

Apply each wallet's locked bounds before aggregation: clamp to [0, total]
for non-negative totals and preserve locked for negative totals. Emit the
summed amounts without re-clamping, deriving free in fixed point to preserve
the balance invariant and expose shortfalls as negative free. Keep margin
requirements separate per wallet because their denominations differ.

Preserve eight-decimal precision for account balances and extend it to the
flex portfolioValue entry. Instrument quote currencies, REST fill
commissions, and resulting PnL resolve standard fiat definitions: EUR and
USD use two decimals, while JPY uses zero. Configuration accepts both venue
and standard codes.

Update the migration guidance for persisted instruments, fills, positions,
and balances, including the previous XBT/XDG aliases and corrupted TZ, RX,
and AUT codes. Correct the prefix-stripping doc comments and add regression
coverage for cross-wallet aggregation, wallet-local bounds, separate margin
entries, and mixed-sign balances.

deltas.subject: Fix Hyperliquid unified account balances (#5187)
deltas.review_summary:
Fix Hyperliquid unified account balances (#5187)

Unified and portfolio margin accounts report every balance and hold in
the spot clearinghouse state. The adapter inferred the mode from the
default-dex perp summary instead. Once positions were open, its negative
totalRawUsd made the perp side look authoritative and the adapter
dropped spot USDC.

Query userAbstraction alongside the two clearinghouse requests and, for
unifiedAccount and portfolioMargin, build balances from spot with spot
USDC hold as the account-wide margin. Other modes keep the existing
logic.

Related to #4206.

* Reject non-string Hyperliquid user abstraction responses

serde_json reads a single-key object such as {"unexpected": null} as a
unit variant, which #[serde(other)] maps to Unknown, so a malformed
userAbstraction response fell back to the perp-summary balances this
change exists to avoid. Only a bare string is accepted now. Any string
still decodes to a known mode or to Unknown.

Regenerate the PyO3 docstring for request_account_state, which had
drifted from the Rust docs.

Add tests for paths nothing covered: an unrecognized mode string keeps
the perp-summary balances through request_account_state, connect fails
when the mode cannot be read, and query_account reaches the
userAbstraction request before going quiet.

Reorder the account docs so the mode split comes first, and state what
happens when the mode cannot be read.

* Clear stale USDC for spot-collateral Hyperliquid accounts

In unified and portfolio margin modes balances come from spot alone, and
the spot parser skips zero-total rows. When spot USDC read zero or its
row was missing, the account state carried no USDC entry. Account
updates keep any currency an update omits, so a previously funded
account kept its old USDC balance and margin.

Always report USDC in these modes, as zero when the spot row is zero or
missing. The non-empty update also replaces the stale USDC margin.

Add a regression that applies a funded snapshot followed by zero-USDC
and missing-USDC snapshots in both modes.

deltas.subject: Scope Kraken spot bulk position coverage to the report source (#5185)
deltas.review_summary:
Scope Kraken spot bulk position coverage to the report source (#5185)

Under `spot_account_type=Margin` the adapter emitted a synthetic FLAT position
report for every cached spot position that Kraken `OpenPositions` did not
return. `OpenPositions` reports leveraged positions only, so an unleveraged lot
can never appear there and its absence is not evidence that it closed. The
engine acted on the FLAT by fabricating a fill, closing the position and
realizing PnL while the coins remained in the wallet.

The same assumption reached the engine a second way: the spot client did not
override `ExecutionClient::provides_bulk_position_coverage`, whose default is
`true`, so an absent report was treated as proof of flat even in cash mode,
where the bulk read returns nothing at all.

Remove the sweep and declare the real coverage, which only the wallet-derived
path provides. Kraken futures is unaffected; its `OpenPositions` is
authoritative for every futures position.

Closes #5181.

* Follow the wallet read when declaring Kraken spot position coverage

The wallet read reports only instruments quoted in
`spot_positions_quote_currency`, so declaring coverage for every instrument in
wallet mode still let an absent report force-close a holding the read could
never have reported.

Make coverage per-instrument and derive it from the read: one shared predicate
holds the bulk branch's instrument-level skips, the HTTP client answers coverage
through it, and the execution client delegates rather than restating the rule
where it could drift.

Documents the filter's reach in the config comment and the integration guide,
which already stated the read's behaviour the code contradicted.

Removing the synthetic FLAT also removed a recovery that was correct for a
leveraged-only margin account, and the PR claimed the closing fill took its
place. It does not. With a lookback declared, a fully closed lot is absent from
`OpenPositions`, so the instrument carries no position report and the engine
projects the closing fill as order-only: the order reaches FILLED while the
cached position keeps its quantity and its realized PnL. A periodic check does
not recover it either, since margin mode declares no bulk position coverage.

That is the shared engine's documented behavior for an instrument with no
in-scope position report, so correct the claim rather than reinstate the sweep,
and state the condition, why the obvious mitigation is incomplete, and what to
run instead.

Adds the startup regression the removal lacked. The existing margin test covers
the periodic entrypoint only; this one reads the startup mass status, asserts no
synthetic FLAT reaches it, pins that the window is declared, and checks the
cached position keeps its quantity and realized PnL.

deltas.subject: Add live bars, depth, and custom data subscriptions to Databento (#5201)
deltas.review_summary:
Add live bars, depth, and custom data subscriptions to Databento (#5201)

The v2 Databento data client had no handler for subscribe_bars,
subscribe_book_depth, or subscribe_data, so those commands logged
"handler not implemented" and delivered nothing. The live decode path
already handled these records.

- subscribe_bars selects ohlcv-1s, ohlcv-1m, ohlcv-1h, or ohlcv-1d
  from the bar aggregation, sharing the mapping with historical bar
  requests. It requires a step of 1 and the LAST price type, the only
  price type the decoder emits.
- subscribe_book_depth subscribes to mbp-10 and rejects an explicit
  depth other than 10.
- subscribe_data subscribes to statistics or imbalance for the
  DatabentoStatistics and DatabentoImbalance data types, with the
  instrument ID as the data type identifier. Emitted records carry
  that identifier, so they publish on the subscriber's topic. It
  rejects data types with metadata, since the records carry none.
- All three accept raw symbols only and reject continuous, parent,
  and instrument ID symbols. Records resolve to the underlying
  contract, so those subscriptions would publish on topics the
  subscriber does not listen on.
- The matching unsubscribe commands are ignored, as for the existing
  subscriptions, because the live API has no granular unsubscribe.

withdrawal, so the account kept the previous balances.

needs a perp summary; a response without one keeps the previous USDC
balance rather than zeroing it. The public spot balance request still
returns non-zero tokens only.

A token the venue drops from the spot state entirely is not covered; it
needs the full-snapshot handling discussed in #5182.

On accounts without spot collateral, a response with no perp summary
still reported the spot rows listed at zero, including a zero USDC row.

cleared its margin.

Clamp Hyperliquid single-order reduce-only reports to fills (#5222)

A single-order status lookup for a closed order dropped `reduceOnly`
from the orderStatus response, although the venue returns it and the
model already reads it. Neither single-order path compared the report
with the order's fills, so a reduce-only stop sized above the
position it closed came back Filled at the venue size, as mass status
did before #5192.

query_order oid fallback, fetch the fills for a reduce-only Filled
report and clamp it with the same helpers and rules as mass status:
only when the fill history is complete and below the venue cap. A
failed fills request, a capped history or an incomplete one keeps the
venue quantity and is logged.

deltas.subject: Round trailing stop prices to the price increment (#5241)
deltas.review_summary:
Round trailing stop prices to the price increment (#5241)

`trailing_stop_calculate_with_last` rounded the calculated price to the
increment's decimal places. On an increment that is not a power of ten,
a basis-point offset, or a price offset that is not a multiple of the
increment, then gave a trigger or limit price between two increments.
The matching engine skipped the fill of a stop that a bar took through
such a trigger, and the emulator released a trailing stop-limit at a
limit price off the increment.

Keep the previous result when it is already a multiple of the
increment, and otherwise round to the nearest multiple, with ties to
even.

The `update_order` guard that validates only changed prices stays for
restored orders, which skip submit validation: name them in its comment
and cover it with a restored stop.
deltas.no_impact_rationale: Rounds calculated trailing-stop prices to the instrument increment; guidance does not teach off-increment derived stops.

deltas.subject: Store full currency records in the Redis cache (#5195)
deltas.review_summary:
Store full currency records in the Redis cache (#5195)

A Redis currency entry held only the bare code, which resolves only in a
process where that code is already registered, and `load_all` decoded
every collection concurrently without registering anything. On restart,
a currency minted at runtime was dropped, along with every instrument,
account, order, and position that referenced it, while startup reported
success.

- Store the same record Postgres does (code, precision, ISO 4217, name,
  and currency type), and keep loading legacy bare-code entries for
  codes that are already registered
- Register currencies before decoding their dependents in every load
  path, without overwriting an existing registration; the cached map
  takes the registered definition and logs a stored record that differs
- Persist an account's balance, margin, and base currencies from
  `add_account` and the account update paths, closing the gap for
  collateral no instrument carries on both backends
- Fail the load on a record that does not decode, describes an invalid
  currency, or sits under another code's key, and log and skip a legacy
  bare code that is not registered
- Read the code as the whole key after the `currencies:` prefix, so
  codes containing the delimiter, such as Hyperliquid HIP-3 `xyz:TSLA`,
  round-trip

`Currency` and `Money` still serialize as bare codes, and
`CurrencyIdentity` stays wallet-only.

Closes #5183.
deltas.no_impact_rationale: Stores complete currency records in Redis instead of relying on names alone; inspected guidance does not prescribe the former currency payload.

deltas.subject: Keep non-reopened voided quantity out of leaves across OrderUpdated (#5133)
deltas.review_summary:
Keep non-reopened voided quantity out of leaves across OrderUpdated (#5133)

Every order type's update() recomputed leaves_qty from quantity and
filled_qty alone, so a non-reopened OrderFillVoided correction became
working again after the next OrderUpdated. OrderCore now caches the
non-reopened voided quantity and applies it consistently; Betfair and
Polymarket report OrderUpdated.quantity gross so the exclusion holds
across adapter-driven updates too.

- Clamp without a warning in `apply_updated_quantity` when a terminal
  reconciliation update at the filled quantity meets a void, and state
  that exception in the OrderUpdated contract
- Serialize `non_reopened_voided_qty` on OrderCore and regenerate the
  canonical backtest digests of every workload that submits orders, in
  both precision modes; replay has no orders and is unchanged
- Subtract earlier Polymarket venue orders' non-reopened voided quantity
  from the venue-leg quantity while the order quantity still covers
  filled plus voided, so a second modify, status reports, and restart
  restore expect the leg actually submitted
- Leave earlier legs' voids out of the filled quantity before a promoted
  replacement leg, and count only each trade's latest fill-void
  revision on a venue leg
- Track the quantity earlier venue orders filled beside their gross
  quantity, so a dust-terminal replacement closes at its filled quantity
  on the buffered, WebSocket MATCHED, FOK taker, modify promotion, and
  order status report paths
- Take the voided quantity out of the terminal status report quantity,
  so a report closes the order when its MATCHED message was missed, and
  count it in the BUY overfill raise
- Reject a Polymarket modify before the cancel when its target does not
  exceed filled plus voided, or when the replacement falls below the lot
  size and would sign for zero shares; check the lot size again after
  the cancel
- Fold Betfair replaced legs after `resolve_ambiguous_replaces` with
  their voided quantities, as the matched-quantity fold does, and
  promote an Accepted successor to PartiallyFilled only when the folded
  fills are non-zero
- Cover a replaced Betfair bet's void through the report task, mass
  status, and the order query, including passes that resolve an
  ambiguous replace of its successor or promote the replace that
  retires it
- Describe the Betfair active size as matched plus remaining plus
  voided, including replaced bets, and show the clamp in
  `order_fill_voided.md`
deltas.no_impact_rationale: Retries transient macOS runner image failures, an internal CI detail.

deltas.subject: Port the Interactive Brokers adapter onto ibapi 5.0.0 (#5041)
deltas.review_summary:
Port the Interactive Brokers adapter onto ibapi 5.0.0 (#5041)

Rewrite the Interactive Brokers adapter against ibapi 5.0.0, replacing
the 3.3.0 API. Keep IB futures parsing in the adapter and preserve futures
and futures-option identifiers based on IB's local symbols.

- Report distinct permanent order IDs sharing one client order reference
  as separate external orders. Cancelling the original still cancels the
  whole group. Hold executions for untracked orders while fetching their
  order details and fills, then emit them together. A failed or empty
  query forwards the held fills unchanged.
- Keep the account summary subscription open after connect so balances
  and margins refresh throughout the session. Complete updates after one
  second without new rows, since IB sends no further End marker. Deliver
  connect, refresh, and query_account results through an execution event
  sender captured on the core thread.
- Collect single-order, bulk-order, fill, and position reports on runtime
  workers through an owned report client. Share collection logic with the
  inline methods to preserve filters, report identity, and errors. While
  disconnected, task hooks return None and inline methods report an
  error. Mass status collection keeps the inline path.
- Clear the instrument book and L2 order ID map on market depth Reset
  notices. Send spread fills after their leg fills so callbacks see leg
  positions and cash already applied. Combo executions no longer wait
  for commission reports, since IB charges commissions on the legs.
  Release a spread fill with a warning if its legs do not arrive within
  five seconds.
- Add generic spread identifiers to the model and allow strategies to
  modify trailing stop triggers. Update bindings, docs, examples, and
  tests for the new adapter API.

Paper-account validation confirms that an ES put spread and its
flattening order each emit both leg fills before the spread fill,
within 2 ms.

Fixes #5193
Fixes #5194
Related to #5216

deltas.subject: Apply backtest funding settlements to positions in place (#5238)
deltas.review_summary:
Apply backtest funding settlements to positions in place (#5238)

SimulatedExchange::settle_funding_rate copies each open position for
valuation, clones it again to apply the funding adjustment, and calls
Cache::update_position, which makes a third copy. Each copy includes
adjustment and replay history that grows with every settlement, giving
O(k) cost per settlement and O(k^2) total cost for a position held
through k settlements.

Use history-free snapshots for valuation and apply adjustments to cached
positions in place through Cache::update_position_from_adjustment,
following update_position_from_fill. If a database update or account
adjustment fails, Cache::revert_position_adjustment restores each
adjusted position from its snapshot and persists the restored state,
preserving the existing rollback behavior.

Validate rollback input before changing position state or history,
rather than relying on debug assertions. Check the position ID, size
precision, settlement currency, and last replay event, then verify that
applying the latest adjustment to the snapshot reproduces the current
state. Reject incompatible PnL currencies and additions outside Money
bounds before applying the adjustment. Validation errors leave the
position unchanged, propagate through Cache::revert_position_adjustment,
and are logged by the funding rollback.

Also reject snapshots older than the adjustment preceding the latest
one. This catches stale snapshots taken before a zero-value adjustment,
which can otherwise leave the restored timestamp older than the retained
history. The check assumes adjustments are applied in timestamp order,
as they are in the backtest.

deltas.subject: Fix Kraken futures single-collateral margin currency (#5199)
deltas.review_summary:
Fix Kraken futures single-collateral margin currency (#5199)

Single-collateral futures margin requirements were labeled USD, so a
0.05 BTC requirement on fi_xbtusd was reported as 0.05 USD. Use the
wallet's required currency field, which Kraken documents as the
denomination of auxiliary and marginRequirements.

Resolve the currency once per wallet and pass it to both parsers.
Without a usable field, omit the margin requirement, report no assets
as locked, and log a warning. Do not infer the denomination from asset
keys, where another asset's dust could produce the wrong currency.
Skip invalid asset keys with a warning rather than panicking.

Sum margin requirements per normalized currency, since MarginAccount
stores account-wide margins by currency and duplicate entries previously
overwrote each other. Preserve eight-decimal precision, including for
flex USD requirements.

Apply auxiliary.af only to the wallet's own currency when deriving
locked balances. Other assets remain unreserved, and contract-symbol
keys remain excluded because they represent positions.

Read flex initial and maintenance margins from the top-level
initialMargin and maintenanceMargin fields. Reading maintenance from
the single-collateral marginRequirements shape previously reported
zero. Emit a requirement when either margin figure is positive.

Add regressions for the documented wallet shapes, per-currency sums,
unresolved currencies, balance reservations, and flex margin fields.
Preserve contract-symbol and zero-wallet coverage, and document account
denominations and precision without narrating superseded behavior.

Closes #5198.

deltas.subject: Generate one account state per funding settlement (#5249)
deltas.review_summary:
Generate one account state per funding settlement (#5249)

The exchange publishes PositionAdjusted for each funding payment.
On margin accounts with calculate_account_state enabled,
Portfolio::update_position recomputed margins and published a duplicate
of the state the balance adjustment had already produced. The account
applied and retained both states.

Skip the margin recompute for adjustments without a quantity change,
since these only change realized PnL. Publish the account's last state
once per state, so a settlement that adjusts several positions still
publishes its account state once.

Build funding balances with MarginAccount::balance_locking_margins,
reusing the rule from recalculate_balance to cap locked margin at the
total and preserve the locked/free balances the recompute produced.
Include both account-wide and per-instrument margins in the state.

deltas.subject: Resolve GreeksCalculator underlying across venues (#5234)
deltas.review_summary:
Resolve GreeksCalculator underlying across venues (#5234)

GreeksCalculator built an option's underlying instrument ID from the
option's own venue. An option listed on a different venue than its
underlying (an IB equity option on AMEX with the stock on NASDAQ) found
no underlying price, so the Python API returned None.

Resolution now follows option expiry settlement. It uses the option's
venue when the cache holds that underlying or a futures spread is cached
for it, and otherwise a unique exact-symbol match from the cache. An
ambiguous match returns an error that names the candidates. With no
match the option's venue is kept, as before.

Cached greeks with no shocks return before the underlying is resolved,
so an ambiguous underlying doesn't block a cached read. A call with
shocks still resolves the underlying for beta weights.

The calculator remembers a unique cross-venue match per underlying
symbol, so repeated instrument_greeks and portfolio_greeks calls don't
rescan the instrument cache. It reuses the match while that instrument
stays cached and drops it once the instrument is purged. The next lookup
then scans again and reports any ambiguity. While a match is remembered,
a same-symbol instrument added on another venue doesn't make it
ambiguous.

Resolves #5137.
deltas.no_impact_rationale: Improves GreeksCalculator underlying resolution across venues; no inspected guidance mandates same-venue-only resolution.

deltas.subject: Validate Kraken Spot L2 book checksums and resync on mismatch (#5219)
deltas.review_summary:
Validate Kraken Spot L2 book checksums and resync on mismatch (#5219)

Validate Kraken Spot L2 snapshots and updates against the venue's CRC32
checksum over the top ten levels on each side. Render prices at
`pair_decimals` and quantities at `lot_decimals`, sharing the inline IEEE
CRC32 and raw formatting with L3. Spot and tokenized instruments carry the
wire price scale when it is finer than tick precision, and validation
reads the current instrument definition on each message.

On a checksum mismatch, emit a `Clear` delta, discard the shadow book,
and resubscribe for an explicit snapshot. Ignore updates until that
snapshot arrives. Three consecutive mismatches disable validation for
the instrument with an error log and retain the received book. Only a
valid update resets the count; a fresh subscription or reconnect resets
validation state.

Bind recovery to the subscription generation and snapshot epoch so stale
work cannot cancel a replacement subscription or disturb a recovered
book. Serialize recovery commands with user subscriptions and include
the depth on unsubscribes. Retain the latest recovery per instrument in
each frame to avoid interleaved unsubscribe and subscribe commands.

Use a snapshot watchdog with exponential backoff and up to five retries.
Subscribe rejections count as failed requests, while stale replies are
ignored. Clear consumer books when recovery or reconnect discards their
shadow state, and remove recovery state when a subscription ends.

Accept snapshots only after the venue confirms the latest subscribe
request. Drop frames from retired streams, and parse each snapshot into
a fresh book before committing state so a parse failure leaves the wait
active. Emit frames with unknown subscription keys as unvalidated deltas
with a one-time warning; quietly drop frames from ended subscriptions.

Enable `validate_l2_checksum` by default and append it after the existing
config arguments to preserve Python positional calls. Update the
generated stubs and replace the hand-written book fixtures with Kraken's
documented example and a derived update.

Closes #5101.

deltas.subject: Fix Interactive Brokers order ID start below used IDs (#5284)
deltas.review_summary:
Fix Interactive Brokers order ID start below used IDs (#5284)

IB refuses an order ID at or below one the same client already used
(error 103), across sessions. On an account shared by several execution
clients, IB's next valid ID can sit in another client's partition, and
the execution client then kept only its last six digits. With no order
open it could start below IDs it had already used, so IB refused every
order until the counter climbed past them.

Start above the highest order ID this client has among IB's completed
orders as well as its open ones. A completed order carries its API order
ID on the order itself; the top-level ID is unset.

Related to #5277

* Fail IB order ID start on incomplete order snapshot

The completed-orders read logged a stream error and kept going, but an
ibapi subscription ends after any error, so startup took the maximum of
an empty or partial snapshot. The request timeout also covered only the
subscription request, so a snapshot without its end marker could stall
startup.

Return the stream error, and bound the request and the read with one
deadline from request_timeout, so either case fails initialization.

Related to #5277

* Fail IB order ID start on dropped order records

When an ibapi order stream falls behind, ibapi drops the oldest records
and sends a lag notice (code -6) in their place. filter_data() discarded
that notice, so the completed-orders read could still return a partial
maximum without error, and startup could reuse an order ID.

Read the snapshot's notices directly: a lag notice fails initialization,
and other notices are still logged and skipped.

Related to #5277

deltas.subject: Fix RiskEngine free balance ignoring unacknowledged orders (#5184)
deltas.review_summary:
Fix RiskEngine free balance ignoring unacknowledged orders (#5184)

Balance checks use the account's free balance, which only reflects orders
the account already locks. Orders approved by earlier commands are not
counted until they reach those states, so buys submitted from one callback
can jointly exceed a cash account's free balance with borrowing disabled.

Retain each approved order's charge against free balance until the cached
order is open or closed, or in flight for a wallet account. Deduct these
reservations when checking subsequent new orders. Release reservations
from cached order status before each command, without relying on order
events, so the cost stays proportional to unacknowledged orders.
Amendments remain checked against the account alone.

Check and reserve wallet buys at the amount the wallet locks: computed
buy costs rounded up at the observed balance precision, or the quote
amount for quote-quantity buys. Retaining instrument notional can cause
raw scale mismatches that deny affordable orders with
NOTIONAL_CALCULATION_FAILED, or lose rounding when scales match and allow
overcommitment. Use the wallet's own funding calculation to preserve both
the funded amount and observed precision, without deduction-time
normalization. Deny reservations whose precision differs from the observed
balance, consistent with wallet locking, and report the funded amount in
wallet buy denials.

Add a regression where a wallet buy reaches Submitted and the portfolio
applies its lock, then approve a second buy that exactly fits the remaining
free balance. The test fails if the risk reservation and wallet lock count
the first order twice.
deltas.no_impact_rationale: Adds a cross-adapter order-book stress harness; no inspected core guidance names an incompatible stress interface.

deltas.subject: Fix Kraken futures orders-status report client order IDs (#5293)
deltas.review_summary:
Fix Kraken futures orders-status report client order IDs (#5293)

Kraken echoes the client order ID submitted by the adapter, which
truncate_cl_ord_id shortens past 18 characters. Reconciliation treats
that value as the full ID, so periodic open-order checks ignore window
reports and startup treats held orders without a venue ID as external.

- Restore each window report's full client order ID from the cache's
  venue order ID index. Otherwise require a unique shortened ID shared
  by one order queried by client ID and one unindexed report, with
  matching instrument and side. Require placement no more than five
  seconds before creation, allowing clock skew while excluding older
  colliding reports.
- Fold duplicate window reports by venue order ID before attribution
  and pricing checks, using the existing history precedence rule:
  closed state, then later update, then larger filled quantity on a
  timestamp tie. Keep this fold scoped to the window reports.
- Withhold reports that cannot be attributed and fully executed window
  reports that lack fill prices, logging the specific reason and
  marking mass status incomplete. Keep canceled reports with executions
  unpriced because cached-order reconciliation waits for their fills.
- Document the attribution and pricing rules, and cover ambiguous IDs,
  instrument and side mismatches, clock-skew boundaries, request bodies,
  completeness, and state, timestamp, and fill-quantity precedence.
deltas.no_impact_rationale: Kraken futures orders-status client order-ID parsing fix; recovery coverage guidance is refreshed with the Kraken integration overlay (ADP-6).

cannot be parsed. Previously, the order was dropped with a completeness

Closed and historical parse failures still mark the set incomplete.

Preserve the exception for untouched reduce-only futures stop and

Exclude skipped triggers from the history read as well, preventing a
zero-quantity placement from being reported as filled. Update the docs
and regression tests to cover lookup scope, position-derived sizing,

Account for IB's commission rules recorded from a paper MES session:

deltas.subject: Fail IB order ID start above client partition (#5306)
deltas.review_summary:
Fail IB order ID start above client partition (#5306)

IB refuses every order ID below a client's next valid ID (error 103).
When that ID lay above the client's partition, the execution client kept
only its last six digits, an ID IB refuses, so every order of the
session was rejected. On an IB paper account, client 7760's next valid
ID is 770000006 and IB refused order 760002000 from it.

Fail initialization in that case with an error naming both IDs, instead
of mapping the ID into the partition. A next valid ID below the
partition is still mapped as before.

Related to #5277.

deltas.subject: Fix Kraken order lookups answering absent from partial reads (#5311)
deltas.review_summary:
Fix Kraken order lookups answering absent from partial reads (#5311)

The single-order lookup on both clients read through wrappers that drop
the completeness flag, so a read that skipped rows or stopped short
could answer Ok(None), which reconciliation takes as the venue having
no such order: an accepted order is rejected, a partially filled one
canceled.

The order reads now return what they covered: the venue order IDs of
the rows they skipped, whether a skipped row named no order, and, when
cut short, from what time on they read everything. A lookup that finds
nothing answers Ok(None) only when that rules the order out, and
otherwise fails, so reconciliation defers. A futures history page with
a continuation token holds the newest events, so it still rules out an
order placed after its oldest event by more than a 60-second clock skew
allowance, taking the earlier of the order's creation and acceptance;
a page with no events, a spot closed-order read stopped at its page
cap, and a skipped row that names no order rule out nothing. Mass
status keeps its completeness flag, now derived from the same value.

Follow-up to #5295.
deltas.no_impact_rationale: Prevents false absence from partial Kraken reads, reinforcing the existing coverage contract.
